# Connect on Product Analytics use cases & insights
Date: 2026-10-05 | Duration: 36.13999938964844m

## Summary
The discussion focused on limited adoption of product analytics caused by overlapping tools, fragmented ownership, and weak organizational standards. Customers often prioritize consolidating feature flagging and experimentation, while product analytics is treated as a bundled bonus, especially when replacing costly tools such as Adobe or Amplitude. Sales should qualify prospects by understanding their current tools, data workflows, ownership, tagging, schemas, and reporting needs, then tailor the pitch around consolidation and savings. Mature enterprises are difficult to convert because of existing investments, while smaller or less mature companies offer stronger opportunities. Amplitude, Mixpanel, Adobe, and PostHog were identified as primary competitors. Warehouse-native analytics, BI integration, controlled data access, and easier migration from similar APIs and schemas are important advantages. Key gaps include real-time analytics and tighter experimentation-to-analytics integration. Planned improvements include real-time telemetry, the populations feature, AI-assisted analysis, and continued sales training.

## Keywords
product analytics, experimentation, feature flagging, platform consolidation, real-time telemetry, sales training

Support the sales team by advising them to consistently ask customers about their current product analytics tools and data logging practices during sales conversations to identify consolidation opportunities (33:35)
